articles.title: Micah Parsons' brother sparks controversy with a comment supporting Josh Jacobs following alleged assault on his girlfriend
articles.standfirst: Parsons’ brother doubles down on his defense of Josh Jacobs despite growing criticism
articles.summary: Parsons’ brother doubles down on his defense of Josh Jacobs despite growing criticism
articles.body:
Terrence Parsons Jr., the older brother of Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons , has attracted significant attention after publicly defending Josh Jacobs amid the running back's ongoing legal troubles.

Jacobs has been charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property in Wisconsin following an alleged incident involving his former girlfriend.

The case has drawn increased scrutiny after authorities indicated that surveillance footage from a garage may support parts of the allegations.

According to the criminal complaint, an argument involving Jacobs ' phone reportedly escalated into a physical confrontation.

The woman alleged that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she attempted to leave. Police reportedly observed redness on her face and neck, along with a bump on the back of her head.

Jacobs hasn't been convicted of either charge, however, and prosecutors have stressed that the charges are accusations rather than proof of guilt. His attorneys have also indicated that the matter will be addressed through the legal process.

The controversy took another turn when Parsons Jr. responded on X to criticism of Jacobs . After one user suggested that the Packers should consider moving on from the running back, Parsons Jr. argued that people were overreacting to the situation.

"A shove? Y'all gotta relax… anger gets the best out of anyone… everyone deserves a second chance… misdemeanors at that," Parsons Jr. wrote.

Parsons Jr. doubles down on Jacobs defense

Rather than backing away from his original position, Parsons Jr. doubled down after facing backlash. He argued that the situation shouldn't be compared with the Ray Rice case and maintained that Jacobs' NFL career shouldn't be put at risk over the allegations.

That comparison added to the debate because Rice's domestic violence case resulted in one of the most notorious disciplinary episodes in NFL history.

Parsons Jr.'s comments have prompted debate about how the league should respond when players face allegations involving violence against women.

It's also important to note that Parsons Jr.'s views don't necessarily represent Micah Parsons or the Green Bay Packers. Terrence has established a public profile of his own and regularly shares strong opinions about NFL-related issues.

The NFL is conducting its own investigation into Jacobs and could impose discipline regardless of the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

Under the league's Personal Conduct Policy, Jacobs could potentially face a suspension or other action if the NFL determines that his conduct violated league rules.

The Packers have acknowledged the charges and said they'll continue cooperating with the NFL's investigation. Jacobs ' availability for the upcoming season could therefore remain uncertain while the league reviews the evidence.

The legal process is ongoing and Jacobs remains presumed innocent. However, the reported surveillance footage and the NFL's independent investigation mean the controversy isn't likely to disappear soon.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs gets sidelined by Roger Goodell and Packers fans have already identified his replacement
articles.standfirst: Jacobs won't be playing football for the foreseeable future, and no one knows how long it will be before he's back.
articles.summary: Jacobs won't be playing football for the foreseeable future, and no one knows how long it will be before he's back.
articles.body:
This week, Green Bay Packers fans began worrying about their star running back, Josh Jacobs , missing games this upcoming season. The full report from Jacobs' domestic violence incident was released, while the running back was ultimately charged with two criminal offenses : Battery and Criminal Damage to Property .

The details were concerning, but because the case is still ongoing and there's no specific timeline for when it will conclude, many assumed Jacobs would be able to continue playing. As it turns out, it's become possible that the NFL has more information regarding the incident - potentially video footage - because the league has taken a strong stance on Jacobs.

Josh Jacobs placed on Commissioner's Exempt List

The NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Sunday. If the list sounds exclusive, it's because it is, but not in a good way. Only NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell can put a player on the list. Once he does, that player can't take part in any of his team's games .

Right now, there's no way of knowing until when Jacobs will be on that list . It could be all season, if the legal process drags on that long . The Packers front office will now have to scramble to find a replacement for Jacobs. With MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks already on the roster, the Packers traded for Kaleb Johnson right after the Jacobs news broke.

But Johnson isn't exactly a lock to stick on the roster for very long. The 83rd overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft barely got on the field as a rookie for the Pittsburgh Steelers , totaling 69 yards on 28 carries throughout last season.

James Conner and Trey Benson make sense for Packers

Packers fans feel the team needs a veteran running back instead. Naturally, that has many urging the front office to pursue a trade for James Conner , who has practically been demoted to third-string on the Arizona Cardinals . While that makes sense in theory, Conner was just placed on Injured Reserve due to a foot injury suffered last season that hasn't fully healed yet.

The Packers could also take a look at Trey Benson , who was cut by the Cardinals a few days ago. Benson is 24 years old and has shown glimpses of his explosiveness, but like Conner has been hampered by injuries lately.

articles.title: Packers in deep trouble: Bad news for Micah Parsons, while Josh Jacobs becomes serious problem
articles.standfirst: Green Bay ruled Parsons out for at least four games, leaving its pass rush without biggest star
articles.summary: Green Bay ruled Parsons out for at least four games, leaving its pass rush without biggest star
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers no longer have to wonder whether Micah Parsons might make a surprise return early in the season. Their star pass rusher is officially out for at least the opening month.

Green Bay moved Parsons to the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list, a roster designation that guarantees he will miss the first four games of the 2026 campaign while continuing his recovery from a torn ACL.

The decision had been increasingly expected, but it still represents a significant blow for a defense built around Parsons ’ ability to pressure quarterbacks and change games from the edge.

Parsons has been realistic throughout his rehabilitation and has resisted attaching himself too firmly to a return date, even with Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys emerging as a popular target.

“I think the people really want Week 6, I just want to come back when I'm feeling like myself again,” Parsons said. “I say Week 6 would be optimistic.”

The possibility of facing his former team naturally adds intrigue, but Parsons has made clear that sentiment won't dictate his recovery.

Week 6 may still be too soon

Parsons said the real benchmark will be how he feels once he is cleared to practice again.

“The [21-day practice] window opens the first week of October, two, three weeks of practice, but the reality is you gotta feel like yourself, you gotta be moving again,” he said.

“I don't wanna go out there and embarrass myself. That's a real feeling. Packer nation, just know, when I come back, it's going to be up.”

That approach reflects the stakes involved for both player and team. Green Bay didn't acquire Parsons as a short-term addition. He's expected to be one of the defining players on the roster and a central part of the defense for years to come.

Rushing him back for one marquee matchup would make little sense if it jeopardized his explosiveness or increased the risk of another setback.

Green Bay has to survive without best pass rusher

Parsons ’ absence leaves the Packers with a much more difficult challenge up front.

Lukas Van Ness will be asked to shoulder a larger role, while veteran Javon Hargrave becomes even more important as Green Bay looks for ways to replace the pressure Parsons normally creates.

There's no true substitute for a player of his caliber, so the solution will have to be collective.

The timing is also awkward because Green Bay is dealing with additional uncertainty elsewhere on the roster, including running back Josh Jacobs being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List .

That puts immediate pressure on the Packers to navigate the opening weeks without two of their biggest names potentially available. The good news is that Parsons hasn't suffered a new setback. The bad news is that the waiting period is now official.

At minimum, Green Bay will play four games without him. Anything beyond that will depend on whether Parsons feels like himself again, and by his own admission, Week 6 remains more hope than guarantee.

articles.title: Gigaclay?! Packers legend Clay Matthews looks completely unrecognizable in dramatic new viral photos
articles.standfirst: Clay Matthews has left NFL fans doing a double take after the former Green Bay Packers star was photographed with a dramatically different appearance
articles.summary: Clay Matthews has left NFL fans doing a double take after the former Green Bay Packers star was photographed with a dramatically different appearance
articles.body:
Clay Matthews is generating plenty of attention online after new photographs showed the former Green Bay Packers linebacker looking almost unrecognizable compared with the player fans remember dominating NFL offenses.

Matthews , now 40, was recently spotted out while grabbing coffee and groceries, wearing a matching dark green outfit and carrying bags back to his vehicle.

While his imposing physique immediately stood out, it was his face that appeared to have undergone the biggest transformation.

The former linebacker was still sporting his trademark long hair, which he wore pulled back into a bun. That familiar feature helped provide at least one connection to the player who became one of the most recognizable defensive stars of his generation.

Beyond the hair, however, Matthews looked markedly different from his playing days.

The photographs prompted speculation about whether the former NFL star had undergone some kind of cosmetic procedure, although there is no confirmation that he has had any work done. The reason for the change in his appearance remains unclear.

What is considerably easier to recognize is Matthews ' imposing build.

Even years after his playing career ended, the former pass rusher still appears to possess the physique of someone who could line up across from an offensive tackle on Sunday. His arms, shoulders and legs looked particularly muscular as he carried his groceries to his car.

That immediately brought back memories of the linebacker who spent a decade terrorizing quarterbacks in Green Bay.

From Packers superstar to one of the franchise's all-time greats

Matthews entered the NFL as the 26th overall pick in the 2009 draft and made an immediate impact with Green Bay .

He recorded 10 sacks as a rookie, earned a Pro Bowl selection and quickly established himself as one of the most dangerous members of the Packers' defense.

His second season was even more impressive. Matthews registered 13.5 sacks in 2010, finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting and played a major role in Green Bay's run to Super Bowl XLV.

The Packers defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 31-25 in that game, giving Matthews the championship that became one of the defining achievements of his career.

He also made one of the most memorable defensive plays of the postseason when his pressure contributed to a crucial fourth-quarter fumble by Steelers running back Rashard Mendenhall .

Green Bay eventually became the defining chapter of Matthews ' career. He spent 10 seasons with the Packers, making six Pro Bowls and establishing himself as the franchise's all-time sack leader since sacks became an official statistic in 1982, with 83.5. The Packers also inducted him into their Hall of Fame in 2024.

Matthews ultimately finished his NFL career with the Los Angeles Rams in 2019. Across 156 regular-season games, he recorded 91.5 sacks, placing him among the NFL's most productive pass rushers since sacks became an official statistic.

His final NFL season came at age 33, meaning he has now been away from the league for several years. Yet the physical presence that made him such a distinctive player clearly has not disappeared.

Matthews has remained connected to the Packers since retirement and continues to be remembered as one of the central figures of the team's successful era under former head coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers .

In 2026, Matthews was again among the nominees for the Pro Football Hall of Fame, although his candidacy ultimately remains separate from his established status in Green Bay.

For longtime NFL fans, however, the latest images are less about Matthews' résumé and more about just how much his appearance has changed.

The long hair is still there. The linebacker-sized frame is still there. But the face underneath that famous hairstyle has clearly changed enough to make social media users look twice.

And while fans can debate exactly what is behind the transformation, one thing appears certain: Matthews may be retired from football, but he has not exactly lost the ability to turn heads.

articles.title: "Stop talking about me": Aaron Rodgers takes aim at former Packers teammates, Shailene Woodley, and Danica Patrick
articles.standfirst: The Steelers quarterback revisited old feuds and two high-profile relationships during a wide-ranging podcast appearance, insisting people should move on from his past
articles.summary: The Steelers quarterback revisited old feuds and two high-profile relationships during a wide-ranging podcast appearance, insisting people should move on from his past
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers has made it clear that he has little interest in allowing old stories about his career and relationships to be rewritten without offering his own version.

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback used a recent appearance on teammate Cam Heyward's "Not Just Football" podcast to address former Green Bay Packers teammates, former partners Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley , and the public narratives that have followed him for years.

The second part of the conversation was released on September 10, with Rodgers discussing his "last rodeo" and reflecting on several controversial chapters of his life.

Rodgers , now 42, did not identify two former Packers teammates by name when discussing players who had previously criticized him. However, the descriptions strongly point toward former Green Bay wide receiver Greg Jennings and tight end Jermichael Finley.

"I had two teammates who spoke out about me years ago, out of everyone I ever played with who said they didn't have a good experience with me," Rodgers said on the Not Just Football podcast.

"One was bitter because he went to another team and never became a player again. The other just wasn't a smart person. And that one hurt more, because I spent so much time with him.

"The night before games, I'd be in his room for an hour going over the plan, the checks, everything I was going to do. I went above and beyond for that guy.

"Both of them, no one cares about what they have to say, which is for most people at this point in my life. No one cares what they have to say until they use my name."

Jennings has been publicly critical of Rodgers on several occasions since leaving Green Bay for Minnesota in 2013. Most recently, he questioned Rodgers' decision to publicly call out Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson for a mistake during practice.

"I've never liked this. He's not doing this to DK [Metcalf]. He's not doing this to Davante Adams," Jennings said last week on Fox Sports' First Things First.

"You don't take something that we can resolve, and I get it, he talked glowingly about Roman… But Roman is listening to that, and immediately, when you hear "that's the second time," it's like a reprimand of like, we didn't even need to know about the first time.

"This has been the issue that I've always had. When we look at Rodgers, it's like, do you ever do anything wrong?"

Finley, meanwhile, criticized Rodgers after Green Bay's disastrous opening game of the 2021 season, when the Packers lost 38-3 to the New Orleans Saints despite Rodgers entering the campaign as the reigning MVP.

"Each offseason you've got to work like it's your last season," the former tight end said on ESPN. "And, I just don't see a work ethic in Aaron Rodgers that I have in previous years."

Rodgers responded to that criticism by producing another MVP-caliber season, ultimately winning the award for the fourth time in his career.

Rodgers turns his attention to his former relationships

The quarterback's comments became even more personal when the conversation shifted from football to his romantic history.

Rodgers dated Patrick , the former NASCAR driver, from 2018 until 2020 before entering a relationship with actress Woodley. He and Woodley became engaged in 2021, but the relationship ended in 2022.

Rodgers offered his own explanation for why both relationships ultimately broke down. Regarding Patrick, he said there was "zero intimacy" and claimed their relationship deteriorated after he did not want to purchase another property with her following their 2019 Malibu home.

He also pushed back against public criticism of his conduct during the relationship, saying Patrick's account of their time together did not reflect his own experience.

Patrick had previously described Rodgers as emotionally abusive in a 2025 interview, while Rodgers has now presented a substantially different account of the relationship.

The Woodley relationship produced another round of revelations. Rodgers claimed their engagement began to unravel shortly after he proposed and alleged that Woodley expressed an interest in being with another man before they married.

He also disputed suggestions that he was responsible for the actress experiencing emotional difficulties following their breakup.

" No one cares what they have to say until they say my name," he said. "I dated two women who nobody gives a f*** about unless they drop my name, and they like to say their version of the history of what actually happened.

"So I'm this monster of a partner and it's just f***ing horses***. Number one: Why are you still talking about me? It's been years."

Rodgers ' remarks have already generated significant reaction, particularly because Woodley has largely kept her distance from the public discussion surrounding their breakup in recent years. People reported that Rodgers' comments focused heavily on his disagreement with how his former relationships have been portrayed.

The timing is notable as Rodgers prepares for what ESPN describes as his 22nd NFL season and his "last rodeo." He returned to Pittsburgh on a one-year contract after starting 16 games for the Steelers in 2025, throwing for 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Rodgers therefore enters the new campaign with his attention ostensibly focused on football, but his latest podcast appearance has once again placed his personal history firmly in the spotlight.

"If you're only relevant by mentioning my name, you should check yourself," Rodgers told Heyward.

For a quarterback who has repeatedly insisted that he wants to control his own narrative, the message was unmistakable: he believes his former teammates and ex-partners should stop revisiting their histories with him, even as he continues to publicly offer his own version of what happened.
